advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Isolate close_ticket failures in ancestor_atomic_submit so a post-merge ticket-op error does not mask the successful land or leave tickets half-closed.
evidence: ABSENCE: no try/except around close_ticket; the merge at line 330 is irreversible but a close_ticket exception makes the whole call raise, so callers cannot distinguish 'merged, ticket-close failed' from 'did not merge'.
advisory.finding: In ancestor_atomic_submit, after a full merge is confirmed, close_ticket is called per member in a loop with no error isolation. If close_ticket raises for one member (a ticket-op failure), the exception propagates out of a function whose stack has ALREADY merged — leaving some members' tickets closed and others open, and signalling failure to the caller for a land that actually succeeded.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap each close_ticket(member_id) in try/except, collect failures, and return 'merged' (or a 'merged_with_close_errors' signal) rather than letting a ticket-op exception unwind a completed merge.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Enforce (or explicitly assert) the fresh-Verified/is_landable precondition inside ancestor_atomic_submit and wire it into drive_to_submit so the direct client.submit is not a competing untested-submit path.
evidence: 227:                 client.submit(wip.change_id)  # drive_to_submit still submits directly; ancestor_atomic_submit is unreferenced in production
ABSENCE: no call to all_members_fresh_verified or is_landable inside ancestor_atomic_submit, and no production call site uses ancestor_atomic_submit.
advisory.finding: ancestor_atomic_submit performs no freshness or tested-SHA re-check before POST /submit; it relies entirely on the caller having invoked all_members_fresh_verified / is_landable first, but that ordering is not enforced in code and the function is not wired into any caller in this diff (drive_to_submit still calls client.submit directly at loop.py:227). A future/direct caller could submit an untested tree, violating the R5 invariant the module documents.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have all_members_fresh_verified return the fetched ChangeInfos (or record freshness in a single pass) so await_fresh_verified does not re-fetch each member after the gate passes.
advisory.finding: await_fresh_verified fetches every member twice per successful poll iteration: all_members_fresh_verified (loop.py:280) fetches each change, then the recording loop (loop.py:306) fetches each change again for the same data. The freshness snapshot recorded is from a second, later fetch that could differ from the one that passed the gate (a narrow TOCTOU) and doubles read traffic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert await_fresh_verified populates wip.tested_shas and wip.verified_at on the success path (not just the boolean return).
evidence: Docstring promises the post-condition: loop.py:295 "Poll until EVERY member carries a fresh `Verified +1` (recording the tested SHA + verified timestamp on `wip`)"
Implementation writes them: loop.py:307 `wip.tested_shas[member_id] = change.get("current_revision")` and loop.py:310 `wip.verified_at[member_id] = approved.get("date") or time_fn()`
Test asserts only the return: test_s2c_submit_held_out.py:62 `assert got is True` — no assertion on wip.tested_shas or wip.verified_at (ABSENCE)
advisory.finding: await_fresh_verified's documented side effect — recording the tested SHA and verified timestamp onto wip — is never asserted; the success test checks only the boolean return, so a regression that returns True without populating wip.tested_shas/wip.verified_at would pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_await_returns_true_when_all_fresh, after the call assert wip.tested_shas['Iok'] == ok['current_revision'] and 'Iok' in wip.verified_at.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a has_fresh_verified case with a Verified +1 present only in the `all` list (no `approved` key) to cover the second acceptance branch.
evidence: Two independent branches in loop.py has_fresh_verified: `if "approved" in verified: return True` and the loop `for entry in verified.get("all") or []: if (entry.get("value") or 0) >= 1: return True`
Fake always sets both when verified=True: _autolander_fakes.py:36-39 `labels["Verified"] = {"approved": {...}, "all": [{"value": 1, ...}]}`

test_has_fresh_verified_reads_current_patchset_vote only uses change_info(verified=True/False), so the `all`-only shape (Verified +1 present in `all` but no `approved` rollup) is never asserted (ABSENCE)
advisory.finding: has_fresh_verified's `all`-list acceptance branch is never exercised: the test fake always emits both an `approved` summary and an `all` entry when verified, so the `approved`-present short-circuit always fires and the `entry.get('value') >= 1` loop path is untested.
